The Nvidia situation is evolving.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has completely changed his view on Nvidia, $NVDA, over the last 7 days.

Last Sunday, Bessent called for a “dramatic shakeup” at Nvidia and said its board needed to hire a new CEO from “outside” the company.

Today, when asked about Jensen Huang returning as CEO, Bessent said:

“Well, Jensen is on the outside now.”

When pressed on whether Jensen Huang should return, Bessent said, “I think we have to see where the buck stops,” clearly leaving the door open.

This comes just 2 days after President Trump publicly said Jensen Huang should “apologize and return.”

Something is happening behind the scenes.

THE BIGGEST THREAT TO THIS MARKET COULD DISAPPEAR AFTER DECEMBER.

That threat is Fed rate hikes.

To understand why it could go away, we first need to understand why the Fed started hiking in the first place.

The Fed is raising rates because inflation is still too high. Core prices rose 0.3% in October for the third month in a row.

The market expects one more 25 bps hike on Dec 9, which would take rates to 4.00–4.25%.

The goal of a rate hike is to make people and companies spend less, so prices stop rising.

But the current market crash is already doing that job.

The S&P 500 just had its 12th worst week since 1953.

It's down 11.6% from its October high and is now about 1% away from wiping out all its gains for 2026.

That's roughly $8 trillion wiped out from US stocks since the peak.

And it's not just stocks. 

Gold is down 34% from its peak, silver is down 64%, and Bitcoin is down 53%.

When people lose this much money this fast, they spend less, borrow less and take fewer risks.

Companies slow down hiring and investment.

That's the same slowdown another rate hike would cause.

THE MARKET IS ALREADY PRICING IT IN.

On Nov 10, traders saw an 11% chance of a bigger 50 bps hike in December. That chance is now almost gone.

At the same time, the chance that the Fed doesn't hike at all in December has gone from zero to about 11–12%.

The pressure from outside is growing too.

President Trump is openly calling for rate cuts, and New York Fed President John Williams has said the situation doesn't call for dramatic action.

WHAT COULD STILL GO WRONG

The risk is that inflation stays hot.

If it does, the Fed may keep hiking into 2027, as some officials like Musalem want.

But even if markets stabilize from here, the wealth already lost will weigh on spending in the months ahead, and that helps cool inflation.

That's why December could be the last hike of this cycle.
